taxonomy:
## Taxonomy of grid-based logic games (from the provided rules only)

### A. Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black squares/frame; bulbs must not illuminate each other; each numbered cell constrains adjacent bulbs.
- **Kurodoko**: Color some cells black so numbered cells count white cells until nearest black cell or frame; numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold rectangles) contain a given number of painted cells; white cells can’t span more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.

### B. Loop / path drawing games (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers; must pass all white-circle cells with area-wise straight/turn consistency; must not pass black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circle cells; white circles require straight-through with a right-angled turn in an adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; must pass arrow cells; wind direction blocks movement against wind; special side-wind bending constraints.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop; must pass all black circles with the circle as midpoint of the straight segment through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each room visited exactly once; in each room loop passes either all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); alternates moon-room then sun-room behavior.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through all “gates” (dotted segments) exactly once; starts/returns to open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order/direction.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbers indicate how many line segments surround a cell.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop; loop must avoid black cells and numbered cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Yosenabe**: Not a loop; included here only if you interpret “movement” as path, but per rules it is circle movement into gray areas (so see section E).  
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki / Makaro / etc.** are not loop-based per the provided rules.

### C. Region partitioning / tiling / block-structure games
- **Chained Block**: Partition into “blocks” of consecutive black cells; each block has one number or “?”; blocks form chains via corner contact; no two blocks in a chain share the same size/shape (up to rotation/mirror).
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; black orthogonally connected cells must form rectangles/squares; white orthogonally connected cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines; each block contains two same-form areas (white and gray) possibly rotated/mirrored; block number equals half the block’s cell count of that color.
- **Evolomino**: Fill board with numbers; each block has same number and size equals the number; same-sized blocks cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Five Cells**: Divide into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers count surrounding lines including outer frame; lines must surround cells and cannot enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill empty cells with numbers; blocks are maximal orthogonally connected regions of equal number; block size equals the number; same-sized blocks cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges; bridge multiplicity ≤2; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; all islands must be continuously linked.
- **Heyawake** (also fits A/C): Rooms with bold borders; constraints on painted/white connectivity and room-spanning.
- **Nurimeizu**: Paint cells to form a maze from S to G using only white cells; bold-bordered rooms must be fully painted or left white; white cells can’t be cut off into loops; rooms containing S, G, ○, △ can’t be painted; no 2×2 or larger monochrome blocks.
- **Nurimisaki**: Circle cells remain white and are “Misaki”; non-circle cells are not Misaki; Misaki white cell has exactly one adjacent white cell; circle numbers count straight-line white cells from Misaki; all white connected; no 2×2 or larger all-white or all-black connectivity.
- **Makaro**: Rooms (bold borders) each contain all numbers up to the room’s cell count starting from 1; arrow cells: biggest number among up to four neighbors points to the arrow target cell; same number cannot be adjacent across rooms.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains only one number equal to its area (cell count).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered “Tiles” are colored; diagonal-line numbers constrain count of black cells to the right or downward along the diagonal’s line/column until boundary/another diagonal-number cell; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold borders) have a number indicating continuous black cells in that room; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones drop straight down, bottom half must be filled with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Sashigane**: Divide into L-shaped blocks (one cell wide); open circles mark the knee; arrow cells point toward the knee; each block has 0–3 marks (arrows/open circles).
- **Satogaeri**: “Countries” are bold-bordered regions; move circles so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Chained Block / Choco Banana / Double Choco / Evolomino / Fillomino / Five Cells / Hashiwokakero / Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki / Makaro / Shikaku / Sto-stone / Sashigane / Satogaeri / Tilepaint** are all fundamentally about block/region structure.

### D. Coloring / shading with connectivity and adjacency rules
- **Hitori**: Color cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurotto**: Color some cells black; circle number equals sum of continuous black cells extending vertically/horizontally from it; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, place a tetromino (4 consecutive squares); similarly shaped rotated/reversed tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares must be connected; no 2×2 or larger colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black wall cells and white regions; numbers indicate size of continuous white cells; each white area has exactly one number; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade cells; each outlined region contains exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; numbered cells cannot be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines has exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares; uncovered white cells must form a rectangle or square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Yajilin** (also loop-based): includes black-cell adjacency restrictions and loop avoidance.
- **Choco Banana** (also region/shape-based): black/white connectivity shape constraints.

### E. Number placement / arithmetic / constraint satisfaction (non-loop)
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row/column/3×3 block contains all 1–9.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; each cell has one digit; numbers are oriented up-down or left-right.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered territories have counts of additional marks; “—” extends >3 horizontally but ≤2 vertically; “|” extends >3 vertically but ≤2 horizontally.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold lines) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils from a tip; pencil is a straight group of cells with tip at one end; line from tip goes through centers; numbered cells give pencil length; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Norinori**: Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares.
- **Hebi**: Place sequential snake numbers 1(head) to 5(tail) in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; viewing-direction constraints with black squares and arrow direction; black squares show nearest-square snake count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally and can turn; lines can’t cross/branch and can’t go through numbered cells.
- **Satogaeri** (also region movement): circle movement with pass-through counts.
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; arrow shows movement direction with tip in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend and don’t cross other circles/arrows; number in a gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas can have any sum but at least one circle must enter some gray area.

### F. “Snake” / ordered sequence games (explicit head-to-tail or directional order)
- **Hebi**: Ordered snake segments 1→5 with territorial non-touching and directional attack constraints.
- **Nagareru**: Loop with wind direction (not a snake, but directionally constrained movement).
- **Yosenabe**: directional movement arrows (not a snake, but ordered by arrow direction).

### G. Mixed loop + region/shape constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop / Masyu / Mid-loop / Moon-or-Sun / Suraromu / Slitherlink / Yajilin**: all are loop games with additional per-room/per-cell constraints.
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki**: maze/white connectivity constraints with rooms and shape restrictions (not loops).

If you want, I can also output this taxonomy as a table (Game → Category tags) using only these rule-derived groupings.
